result:
Typecheck passes, `bun test` is 4/4 green, and `guren check` reports 0 failures (only pre-existing warnings about missing test files for other controllers).

`PostController.update()` was hand-building its redirect as `new Response(null, { status: 302, ... })`. A 302 tells the browser to replay the *same* method at the new location, so Inertia's `PUT /posts/:id` was answered with a redirect back to `PUT /posts/:id` — an infinite loop that surfaced as `ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS`, while the update itself had already committed (hence the edit appearing on reload). I replaced it with `this.redirect(\`/posts/${post.id}\`)` in `app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts:96`, which uses the framework's non-GET default of **303 See Other** — the same helper `store()` and `destroy()` already use — so the follow-up request is a GET of the post page. Validation still throws before the redirect, so 422 responses on the edit form are unchanged. I also added two cases to `tests/PostController.test.ts`: one asserting a 303 with `Location: /posts/<id>` after a successful authenticated save, and one asserting an empty payload still returns 422, with a `beforeEach` that calls `resetDatabase()` and seeds an author plus a post.
